newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 26.

text.p: The chief executive of Australian Rugby League team Penrith, Mark Levy, foresees the rivalry between the Australian Rugby League and Super League continuing into next season. His earliest prediction for a return to a united competition is 1999. Page 28.

Yesterday's Super League match between North Queensland and the Brisbane Broncos ended in a 20-20 draw. In an entertaining game, the North Queensland team managed to draw level with the Broncos in the last three minutes of play time, with two converted tries giving them an extra competition point. Page 28. --

The match yesterday between Australian Rugby League teams South Sydney and Illawarra ended with a 28-28 draw. In a close fought game, Illawarra lost an 18-6 lead to South Sydney in the second half before managing to draw level again in the closing minute of the game. Page 28.

The future of Australian Cricket team captain Mark Taylor is in serious doubt following his poor batting performance in Australia's Ashes tour of England. Taylor has been stood down from today's third one-day international against England after only scoring seven and 11 runs in the first two one-day matches. Page Sports 2.

The coach of the Australian Football League team North Melbourne, Denis Pagan, yesterday warned several of the team's long standing players against complacency about their performances. He is believed to have been specifically speaking about those player who were signed on long-term contracts following last year's premiership win. Page Sports 3.

A prominent player in the Australian Football League, West Coast team member Chris Lewis has his professional future under a cloud following two recent incidents in which he was reported for violence. The incidents occurred in West Coast's match against ssendon yesterday at Subiaco Oval. Page Sports 3.

The coach of the Australian Football League team Richmond, Robert Walls, has lashed out angrily at his players accusing them of not trying hard enough and not being up to scratch. The comments came after St Kilda's decisive 47 point win over Richmond last night at Waverley Park. Page 96.

Controversy has been sparked within the Australian Football League by comments from Western Bulldogs coach Terry Wallace about changes to the umpire system. He has suggested the senior core of field umpires start "doubling up" for weekend matches. Page 94.

Brisbane team chairman Noel Gordon yesterday criticised what he claimed was the mediocre performance of Australian Football League umpires. He was referring specifically to the umpire decisions made in the Brisbane-Fremantle game held on the weekend, whih were crucial in ensuring victory for Fremantle. Page 94.

Australian basketball received the news last night that Australian forward Mark Bradtke, who has recently been playing in the US, would be playing for the national team in tonight's match against Croatia. Bradtke's availability had been in doubt due to avirus infection which has kept him out of the first three games of the international series. Page 94.

Commentators are uneasy about the future of the Victorian State teams in the Australian Football League competition. Doubts as to their long-term viability have been raised by the success of non-Victorian teams in this year's competition. Page 94.

Australian Football League team the Sydney Swans last night rewarded their fans with a win over Collingwood at the Sydney Cricket Ground. The win was the latest in the extraordinary success the Swans have had at that venue, not losing a game their in the past two seasons. Page 32.

Commentators have predicted long odds for the Australian Capital Territory Brumbies defeating their opponents Auckland at next Saturday's Super 12 rugby union final at Eden Park. Particular concern has been expressed about the Australian side's propensity to commit basic errors which will leave them wide open to the unrivalled professionalism of the Auckland team. Page 33.

Basketball team the Sydney Kings suffered an 11-point lost to the Adelaide 36ers last night. The loss effectively dashes their hopes of winning this year's National Basketball League championship, to be decided in November. Page 34.

Australian Glenn Seton yesterday won all three heats in the sixth round of the Shell Australian Touring Car Championship at Sydney's Eastern Creek venue. The win continues the remarkable domestic and international success Seton has enjoyed this year. Page 34.
